title: Fly between-animal synapse count excess is left-right variation plus a bilateral part; the bilateral part is near zero between two male FIB-SEM nerve cords and does not come from synapse detection
abstract: Question: earlier SCI studies found that gain-corrected synapse count differences between adult fly connectomes repeat on both sides of the animal. Is this bilateral part biology or a dataset effect? Approach: we matched neurons in five connectomes: MANC and the male CNS nerve cord (both male, FIB-SEM), BANC (female, TEM), FAFB (female, TEM) and the right hemibrain (female, FIB-SEM). Two datasets also have two synapse tables on one segmentation. For each pair of copies we cross-fitted per-neuron gains and split the extra-Poisson variance of the log count ratio into a part shared by the left and right sides (cross-side covariance, free of Poisson noise) and a side-specific part, with paired identity bootstraps. Results (connections with a reference mean of 16 or more synapses): in all six animal pairs, the side-specific part equalled the mean within-animal left-right excess (differences -0.010 to +0.017). Synapse-table swaps gave a shared part of 0.001 to 0.011, while animal pairs with a TEM dataset gave 0.26 to 0.42. MANC against the male CNS nerve cord gave a shared part of 0.035 (95% interval 0.018 to 0.061), against 0.260 and 0.283 for the pairs with BANC. Removal of annotated dimorphic neurons and a neuropil factor did not change this. On the right central brain, the FIB-SEM pair (male CNS against hemibrain, different sex) had an excess of 0.348, similar to the cross-method pairs (0.317, 0.363) and 0.07 to 0.12 above the within-animal baseline. Main limitations: one animal per dataset, so sex, pipeline, proofreading and matching are confounded; male CNS nerve cord types were assigned with MANC as reference; the brain and nerve cord results differ and are not resolved.

display.caption: Between-animal extra-Poisson variance split into a part shared by both sides (orange) and a side-specific part (blue), with the mean within-animal left-right excess (dashed), for nerve cord and central brain animal pairs and synapse-table swaps.

(A) Right central brain: within-animal left-right excess and three animal pairs that differ in method only, sex only, or both. (B) Left-right correlation of the extra-Poisson part by connection strength.

We test whether its bilateral between-animal component is a dataset effect.
Its direction-balance bilateral result shares the same animal pairs.
